$comment: Save-worthy, evergreen: a Jev-flavoured checklist for grading ANY AI vendor benchmark claim, not a Jev-specific stat recap (avoids repeating the already-published 'nine ways Jev fails' post). Facts: vendor 193x vs Every's independent 25x (777 decisions/37 docs, 0.35s vs 8.83s Fable 5.1) already verified+published; HN independent-critique framing (model-consensus vs ground truth) already verified+published. No new figures beyond what's already Coach-approved.
title: Should you repeat that *claim?*
sub: Every AI vendor's Nx-faster number this week traces to the same four questions. Run it through them before you cite it.

decisions.name: Who ran the test?
decisions.ask: State = the claim's source line and methodology note.
decisions.route: vendor or UNRESOLVED: cite it as a claim, never a fact.

decisions.name: Ground truth, or model consensus?
decisions.ask: Consensus scores agreement between models, not correctness.
decisions.route: model_consensus: the multiple only says how alike two models are.

decisions.name: Does the outside test beat the inside one?
decisions.ask: One real case: outside 25x, vendor's own peak claim 193x.
decisions.route: outside_higher_or_equal: the two tests likely aren't measuring the same thing.

decisions.name: Would it survive your own labels?
decisions.ask: A wrong repost costs the post's credibility, not a fee.
decisions.route: Lean no: re-measure before you publish the number.

bands.caption: Your own bar, not the vendor's. Re-derive it per claim.

never: NEVER REPEAT: a vendor's own multiple with no outside test · an accuracy % with no stated ground truth · a cost number from one task type.
source: case: Every vs TypeSafe, 777 decisions/37 docs · method: Anton Vnukov
